page: Microsoft Azure HX176-144rs is a high-performance computing instance powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The configuration provides 144 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 1408.0 GB of system memory, delivering approximately 9.78 GB of RAM per vCPU core. Designed for clustered and parallel architectures, the platform includes RDMA networking capabilities alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage.

Local scratch capacity is addressed through 4355 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage, providing high-capacity storage for intermediate data sets and I/O-intensive scratch routines. The server provision includes zero GPUs, orienting all compute power toward dense CPU instructions and memory operations. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, aligning with deployment models that position HPC nodes within private clustered subnets.

Given the combination of 144 dedicated physical cores, a high memory-to-core ratio, integrated high-speed NVMe storage, and RDMA interconnects, the HX176-144rs is configured for memory-intensive engineering simulations, scientific computing, in-memory databases, and large-scale data modeling pipelines.
